The shutters creak open…

Prices follow the Realm Market Exchange and move every 15 minutes, so the same shop costs a little more or less later in the session. The current shop is kept in this browser so a refresh won't lose it, and it never leaves your device. 💾 Back up everything to keep it safe.
The address bar holds the shop's dice seed: 🔗 Copy Link shares the same shop and stock (at the prices of the moment, haggle not included), and Back returns to the previous shop.

How the Shop Generator works

Pick a shop type and how well business is going, or leave both on 🎲. There are thirty kinds of shop, from the General Store and the Blacksmith & Armorer to the Bakery, the Gambling Den, the Barber-Surgeon & Bathhouse, the Guildhall & Mercenaries, and the Monster Parts Dealer. Every roll names the shop and puts a keeper behind the counter, with looks, a voice, a trait, a flaw, and a secret, plus what the shop offers, what it buys, what's on sale, and a job if the party thinks to ask. Stock comes from Player Core, Player Core 2, and GM Core, common items only, priced from the Realm Market Exchange. Wealth sets the highest item level on the shelves: 2 for a Humble shop, 6 for a Modest one, 12 for a Prosperous one, the way a settlement's level does. A Humble shop also carries less and charges under list price; a Prosperous one charges a quarter over. The core books don't price food, livestock, or wagons, so those come at the Gazette's own prices.

At the table

  • The party walks into a town you didn't prep. Roll the shop they asked for and read the greeting out loud while you skim the keeper's secret.
  • A player wants a discount. Type in their Diplomacy bonus and roll against the shopkeeper's Will DC, one try per shop. A success takes 10% off, a critical success 20%, and a critical failure puts the prices up.
  • The party hit level 7 and wants runes. A Modest shop tops out at level 6, so send them to the city, or roll a Prosperous shop and watch the gold go.
  • 🔗 Copy Link saves the exact shop for next session, when the rogue comes back to fence the necklace.

Works with

The Market Exchange sets the prices, the NPC Generator rolls the rest of the town, the Loot Generator fills the party's purse first, and the Settlement Generator lists every shop in a town, each one opening here.
